      "unified_diff": "--- a/MD.root.md\n+++ b/MD.root.md\n@@ -94,6 +94,45 @@\n   are still classifiable when a digit's distinguishing topology can be inferred;\n   abstain only when no candidate has a clear distinguishing cue.\n \n+## Compact/lookalike stroke-program priority\n+For compact, thick, or faint glyphs, decide from the whole intended stroke\n+program, not from one isolated cue such as \u201cthere is a loop,\u201d \u201cthere is a top\n+segment,\u201d or \u201cthere is one vertical stroke.\u201d A claimed cue must have the right\n+role and position in the digit, not merely the same local shape.\n+\n+Canonical boundary checks:\n+\n+- **2 over accidental 0/9 readings:** a rounded upper curve flowing into a\n+  descending diagonal and then into a lower horizontal or near-horizontal\n+  base/terminal is a 2, even if the upper curve nearly closes or thick pixels\n+  form a loop-like blob. Use 0/6/9 only when the closed loop is the dominant\n+  structure and the stroke does not continue into a 2-like lower base.\n+- **4 over 5 when the bar is mid-height:** a 4 has a mid-level crossbar joining a\n+  left slanted/vertical stroke to a straight right stem, usually with the right\n+  stem continuing below the bar and an open or angular upper wedge. Do not treat\n+  this mid-crossbar/right-stem arrangement as the top cap of a 5. A 5's flat bar\n+  sits at the top and is followed by a left stem and one lower right-facing\n+  bowl/hook.\n+- **5 over 1/7 when a lower hook or bowl is present:** a 1 is a single simple\n+  stroke with at most serifs, and a 7 is a top bar plus one descending diagonal\n+  with no lower bowl or hook. If a top cap is followed by a drop/stem and a\n+  curved lower hook or bowl, prefer 5 even when the glyph is narrow, angular, or\n+  compressed. Prefer 6 instead only when the stroke is a continuous curl that\n+  encloses a lower loop, not merely a 5-like bowl bending back toward the stem.\n+- **6/9 over 0/1 when a free tail and loop placement are visible:** a 6 has a low\n+  loop plus an open upper curl/terminal; a 9 has a high loop plus a descending\n+  tail. A 0 has no free tail and is primarily a centered oval; a 1 has no\n+  rounded enclosed head. Do not collapse a 6 or 9 to 0 or 1 just because the tail\n+  is close to the loop, thin, or partially merged by rasterization.\n+- **8 over 9 when the lower part is a lobe:** below a central waist, a rounded\n+  lower portion that closes or near-closes as its own lobe is the second lobe of\n+  an 8, not a 9 tail. A 9's tail is a non-enclosing extension descending from a\n+  single upper loop.\n+\n+Apply these priorities only to visible or inferable stroke structure; do not\n+invent missing bases, bowls, loops, or tails when the surrounding geometry does\n+not support them.\n+\n ## Label hierarchy\n - `digit`\n   - [[MD.digit.0|0 \u2014 single closed loop]]\n"
